newsitem.title: USA: N.H. governor will seek Republican chair.
newsitem.headline: N.H. governor will seek Republican chair.

text.p: New Hampshire Gov. Stephen Merrill said Tuesday he would try to become the next chairman of the Republican National Party.
Merrill, 50, who served two terms as governor but chose not to seek a third, told a news conference he is not the frontrunner and the only "outsider" in the race to succeed Haley Barbour.
But he made more than 130 campaign stops across the country in 1996 campaigning for Bob Dole for president and for the Republican ticket.
"Many of the other candidates may be truely regional, meaning that they want to get states around them and that's the only base they will have," Merrill told reporters in Concord, New Hampshire.
"Because I have visited so many states around the country, I am hoping that my support will be very broad and literally from across the country."

Merrill, a fiscal conservative who kept his pledge not to raise taxes, is the best known of a number of Republicans running for the job. He headed Bob Dole's campaign in the state during the New Hampshire primary, which Dole lost.
Three Republican National Committee members from each state, the District of Columbia, and four U.S. territories will vote Jan. 17 to decide who gets the job.
